models.title: ACCEPTING THE LIFT STATION AND FORCE MAIN AND SANITARY SEWER PUBLIC IMPROVEMENTS FOR ALTON PLACE, SECTION 1, PHASE 1 AND 2 AND THE ALTON PLACE VILLAGE CENTER COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT.
models.text:
Resolution: 26-R-74   Adopted: August 24, 2026   Effective: August 24, 2026
ACCEPTING THE LIFT STATION AND FORCE MAIN AND SANITARY SEWER PUBLIC IMPROVEMENTS FOR ALTON PLACE, SECTION 1, PHASE 1 AND 2 AND THE ALTON PLACE VILLAGE CENTER COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT.

WHEREAS, Alton Place LLC, (the "Developer"), owns (the "Property") located on the west side of Alton Darby Rd both north and south of Roberts Rd as depicted on Exhibit A. The Property includes the Alton Place, Section 1, Phase 1 and Phase 2 (per sanitary sewer plan) residential development and the Alton Place Village Center commercial development; and
WHEREAS, as part of the development plans for the Alton Place, Section 1, Phase 1 and Phase 2 (per sanitary sewer plan) residential development and the Alton Place Village Center commercial development, the Developer is required to build a public sewer system that includes gravity sewers and a sanitary pump station and force main to serve these developments; and
WHEREAS, the public improvements for the following projects have been found to be constructed per the plans submitted to and approved by the City Engineer and are shown is Exhibit B. Alton Place Lift Station and Force Main project (P00958) Alton Place Section 1 Phase 1 & 2 sanitary sewer project (P00959) Alton Place - Village Center public sanitary sewer (P01004); and
WHEREAS, per Section 1191-01 of the City's Planning and Zoning Code, the developer has posed maintenance surety for the public improvements, and the public improvements will be maintained under warranty by the Developer for one year from the effective date of this resolution for final acceptance and full maintenance by the City of Hilliard; and
WHEREAS, it is in the best interest of the City of Hilliard and the public at large that the City accepts the public improvements as noted above.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Hilliard, Ohio:

SECTION 1. The City of Hilliard accepts the public sanitary sewer improvements for Alton Place Sewer Lift Station and Force Main, Alton Place Section 1 Phase 1 & 2 sanitary sewer, and Alton Place Village Center public sanitary sewer, approved by the City Engineer, which are on file in the office of the City Engineer and available for inspection.
SECTION 2. The City Manager, Clerk of Council and City Engineer are authorized to do all acts and to execute all instruments appropriate or necessary to carrying out the terms of accepting the public improvements as provided herein.
SECTION 3. This Resolution shall be effective upon its adoption.

ATTEST: ________________________________ Diane C. Werbrich, MMC, Clerk of Council
SIGNED: ________________________________ President of Council
APPROVED AS TO FORM: ________________________________ Thaddeus M. Boggs, Director of Law

models.title: AUTHORIZING THE CONDITIONAL USE FOR A HEALTH AND FITNESS FACILITY AT 4402 WEAVER COURT NORTH KNOWN AS THE TRAINING COLLECTIVE WITHIN THE M-1, LIMITED INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT.
models.text:
Resolution: 26-R-86   Adopted:   Effective:
AUTHORIZING THE CONDITIONAL USE FOR A HEALTH AND FITNESS FACILITY AT 4402 WEAVER COURT NORTH KNOWN AS THE TRAINING COLLECTIVE WITHIN THE M-1, LIMITED INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT.

WHEREAS, on January 24, 2022, City Council approved amendments to Chapters 1107 and 1123 of the City's Codified Ordinances to state that the Planning and Zoning Commission provides a recommendation to City Council on each conditional use application and that City Council would have the final approval for each application; and
WHEREAS, on March 24, 2025, City Council approved Resolution No. 25-R-27 authorizing the conditional use for a health and fitness facility at 4402 Weaver Court North known as the National Basketball Academy within the M-1 Restricted Industrial District; and
WHEREAS, on July 8, 2026, a completed application for the review of an expansion of a conditional use for "Health and Fitness Facility" for the property at 4402 Weaver Court North (Parcel #050-002994) was submitted to the Planning Director in accordance with Hilliard Code Section 1123.02; and
WHEREAS, the Planning and Zoning Commission on August 13, 2026, reviewed the request for the expansion of a conditional use to permit "Health and Fitness Facility" within the M-1, Restricted Industrial District, for the property located at 4402 Weaver Court North under the provisions of Hilliard Code Section 1123.03 and 1123.04; and
WHEREAS, the Planning and Zoning Commission in accordance with the Code made a positive recommendation to City Council; and
WHEREAS, as prescribed by Section 1107.03(d) upon receipt of a recommendation from the Planning and Zoning Commission, the City Council shall decide upon the conditional use application according to the procedures set forth in Chapter 1123.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Hilliard, Ohio:

SECTION 1. Como Development and The Training Collective (Parcel #050-002994) are granted a conditional use for "Health and Fitness Facility" and will comply with the provisions of Hilliard Code Chapter 1123 and conditions of approval as set forth by the Planning and Zoning Commission.
SECTION 2. Failure to obtain any necessary Zoning Certificate or Certificate of Occupancy shall invalidate the Conditional Use approval granted by City Council.
SECTION 3. This Conditional Use approval in accordance with Section 1123.05 of the Hilliard City Code shall expire 12 months after it is granted, unless construction is complete or commencement of the use has begun, or significant progress has been made towards its initiation.
SECTION 4. Any expansion of the approved Conditional Use requires a final determination by City Council in accordance with Hilliard Code Chapter 1123.
SECTION 5. The Planning Director, City Engineer, and Director of Building Standards are authorized to approve any necessary administrative changes to the approved site plan necessary to carry out the terms of this conditional use.
SECTION 6. This Resolution shall be effective upon its adoption.

models.title: AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO A PURCHASE AGREEMENT WITH UTILITY TRUCK EQUIPMENT, INC., FOR A BUCKET TRUCK THROUGH THE OHIO STATE TERM SCHEDULE (STS) COOPERATIVE PURCHASING PROGRAM; AUTHORIZING THE DIRECTOR OF FINANCE TO ENTER INTO A FINANCING AGREEMENT WITH KS STATEBANK FOR THE PAYMENT OF THE BUCKET TRUCK; AND AUTHORIZING AN EXPENDITURE.
models.text:
Resolution: 26-R-68   Adopted: July 13, 2026   Effective: July 13, 2026
AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO A PURCHASE AGREEMENT WITH UTILITY TRUCK EQUIPMENT, INC., FOR A BUCKET TRUCK THROUGH THE OHIO STATE TERM SCHEDULE (STS) COOPERATIVE PURCHASING PROGRAM; AUTHORIZING THE DIRECTOR OF FINANCE TO ENTER INTO A FINANCING AGREEMENT WITH KS STATEBANK FOR THE PAYMENT OF THE BUCKET TRUCK; AND AUTHORIZING AN EXPENDITURE.

WHEREAS, it is necessary for the health, safety, and welfare of the citizens of Hilliard, Ohio that the City appropriately maintain capital vehicle and equipment fleet; and
WHEREAS, the City Manager has determined that capital vehicles and equipment are needed to perform city programs and services efficiently and effectively; and
WHEREAS, the City desires to purchase a bucket truck from Utility Truck Equipment, Inc. to reduce the overall age of the City's fleet in order to create long-term operational savings, increase employee safety and productivity, and reduce the overall fleet budget over time; and
WHEREAS, in accordance with Ohio Revised Code Section 9.48, the City is permitted to purchase a bucket truck through Utility Truck Equipment, Inc., an approved vendor with the Ohio State Term Schedule (STS) Contract, a cooperate purchasing program of which the City is a member; and
WHEREAS, in order to finance the purchase, the Director of Finance has determined that entering into a Financing Agreement with KS StateBank which provides that the bucket truck be paid for over five years, starting in 2027; and
WHEREAS, Ohio Revised Code Section 5705.44 provides that when a contract runs beyond the fiscal year in which it is made, the fiscal officer shall make a certification for the amount required to meet the obligation of the contract in the current fiscal year, and the remaining amount of the obligation under such contract shall be included in the annual appropriation measure for the subsequent fiscal years; and
WHEREAS, as required by Ohio Revised Code Section 5705.44, the City will require that City Council appropriate funds for financing of the bucket truck in the City's 2027-2031 Capital Improvements Budgets; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Hilliard, Ohio:

SECTION 1. The City Manager is hereby authorized to enter into a Purchase Agreement, attached hereto as "Exhibit A" and incorporated herein, for the bucket truck with Utility Truck Equipment, Inc., an authorized vendor with the Ohio State Term Schedule (STS) Cooperative Purchasing Program, of which the City is a member.
SECTION 2. Future expenditures are authorized in the Capital Improvement Budgets from Fund 304, in years 2027-2031 for the purchase of the bucket truck.
SECTION 3. The Director of Finance is authorized to enter into a Financing Agreement, attached hereto as "Exhibit B" and incorporated herein, for the financing of the purchase of the bucket truck with KS StateBank. The Director of Finance is authorized to approve any necessary administrative changes to the Financing Agreement to affect the proper form and execution of the Financing Agreement in order to finalize the purchase of the bucket truck.
SECTION 4. The City Manager is authorized to sign and execute all necessary agreements to effectuate the purchase, lease, maintenance and sale of capital vehicles and equipment.
SECTION 5. The Finance Director is authorized to make any accounting changes to revise the funding source for any contract or contract modification associated with expenditure of the funds.
SECTION 6. This Resolution shall be effective upon its adoption.

SIGNED: ________________________________ President of Council
APPROVED AS TO FORM: ________________________________ Thaddeus M. Boggs, Director of Law

models.title: AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH AMERICAN STRUCTUREPOINT, INC. FOR THE CITY'S PEDESTRIAN/BICYCLE MOBILITY AND SAFETY PROGRAM (CIP T-133) AND AUTHORIZING AN EXPENDITURE.
models.text:
Resolution: 26-R-88   Adopted:   Effective:
AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH AMERICAN STRUCTUREPOINT, INC. FOR THE CITY'S PEDESTRIAN/BICYCLE MOBILITY AND SAFETY PROGRAM (CIP T-133) AND AUTHORIZING AN EXPENDITURE.

WHEREAS, the City of Hilliard's Engineering Department utilizes the services of consultants to provide on-call services and technical expertise to support the needs of the Department; and
WHEREAS, American Structurepoint, Inc. (ASI) was selected to provide professional services for the City's annual Pedestrian & Bicycle Mobility & Safety Program (hereinafter the "Program") based on their project understanding, technical experience, training, and past performance; and
WHEREAS, the City of Hilliard desires to enter into a professional services agreement (PSA) with ASI for planning, engineering, surveying, and related services for the Program; and
WHEREAS, the PSA is a general engineering services task-order contract, and tasks are performed on an "as-directed" basis, whereby ASI will provide services only as requested and directed by the City based on specific work to be performed; and
WHEREAS, the scope of services for Task 1 of the PSA, which consists of design of the Hayden Run Central Ohio Greenways (COG) Trail between Eventing Way and Avery Road, is provided in Exhibit A; and
WHEREAS, the estimated cost to perform the scope of services for Task 1 - Hayden Run COG Trail is $298,741; and
WHEREAS, by passage of Ordinance No. 25-29 on November 10, 2025, funds in the amount of $300,000 were appropriated in the 2026 Capital Budget for CIP T-133 Pedestrian/Bicycle Mobility & Safety Program to cover the estimated cost for Task 1 - Hayden Run COG Trail; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 3.10 of the Charter of the City, authorization to fund the Services may be established by Resolution of Council.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Hilliard, Ohio:

SECTION 1. An expenditure is authorized in an amount not to exceed $300,000 from Fund 304, Object 55.
SECTION 2. The City Manager is hereby authorized to enter into a professional services agreement ("Agreement") with American Structurepoint, Inc. in substantially the same form as the one attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein, for CIP T-133 Pedestrian/Bicycle Mobility & Safety Program. The City Manager is authorized to make such changes to the Agreement that are not inconsistent with this Resolution and not adverse to the City.
SECTION 3. The City Manager is authorized to modify this Agreement to include additional tasks for up to four additional years, subject to satisfactory performance and the appropriation of sufficient funds by City Council.
SECTION 4. The Finance Director is authorized to make any accounting changes to revise the funding source for any contract or contract modification associated with the expenditure of the funds provided herein.
SECTION 5. This Resolution shall be effective upon its adoption.

models.title: AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO TRANSFER OWNERSHIP OF CERTAIN CITY-OWNED PARCELS IN THE BIG DARBY WATERSHED REGION TO THE COLUMBUS AND FRANKLIN COUNTY METROPOLITAN PARK DISTRICT...
models.text:
Ordinance: 26-22   Passed:   Effective:
AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO TRANSFER OWNERSHIP OF CERTAIN CITY-OWNED PARCELS IN THE BIG DARBY WATERSHED REGION TO THE COLUMBUS AND FRANKLIN COUNTY METROPOLITAN PARK DISTRICT FOR THE EXPANSION OF HOMESTEAD METRO PARK, AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR THE OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF THE HERITAGE TRAIL AND OTHER REGIONAL TRAILS, AND AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENTS WITH M/I HOMES OF CENTRAL OHIO TO AUTHORIZE THE TRANSFER OF CONSERVATION OPEN SPACE FOR THE ENLARGEMENT OF HOMESTEAD METRO PARK.

WHEREAS, by the passage of Resolution No. 23-R-28, City Council accepted the 2023 Community Plan, which set forth "8 Big Ideas" to guide future growth and community priorities, including the creation of a greenbelt of preserved open space along the City's western edge within the Big Darby Creek watershed; and
WHEREAS, the Columbus and Franklin County Metropolitan Park District ("Metro Parks") owns and operates Homestead Metro Park, as well as the Heritage Trail north of Hayden Run Road, and has the capacity to effectively and efficiently maintain, operate, and patrol additional sections of the Heritage Trail currently managed by the City of Hilliard; and
WHEREAS, the City and Metro Parks enjoy a cooperative relationship and have negotiated the terms of a Memorandum of Understanding (the "MOU"), attached hereto as Exhibit "A" establishing guidelines for Metro Parks' operation and maintenance of designated trails as shown via a dashed green line in Exhibit "B"; and
WHEREAS, on June 12, 2026, the Planning and Zoning Commission approved a 2.244-acre lot split of Parcel Number 050-011532 to enable the City to retain ownership of the land on which the water tower is situated; and
WHEREAS, the City will retain utility easements on parcel 050-011532; and
WHEREAS, on June 8, 2026 by passage of Ordinance No. 26-14, Hilliard City Council authorized a Development Agreement with Grand Communities for the Clover Meadows development and authorized the transfer of 35 acres +/- of Conservation Open Space along the Clover Groff directly to Metro Parks.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Council of the City of Hilliard, Ohio:

SECTION 1. City Council hereby accepts the City Manager's recommendation to transfer ownership of the Elliott Road Parcel, identified as Franklin County Parcel Number 120-000173-00, and a portion of the Barbeau Lane Parcel, identified as Franklin County Parcel Number 050-011532 less the 2.244-acre lot split approved by the Planning and Zoning Commission on June 12, 2026, to the Columbus and Franklin County Metropolitan Park District and authorizes the City Manager to sign all necessary agreements to execute these property transfers.
SECTION 2. The City Manager is authorized to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Columbus and Franklin County Metropolitan Park District, attached as Exhibit "A" establishing the terms by which Metro Parks shall operate, maintain, and patrol the Heritage Trail, the Homestead Neighborhood Connector Trail, and the planned regional trail extension through the Hill Farm Development to Scioto Darby Creek Road.

APPROVED AS TO FORM: ________________________________ Thaddeus M. Boggs, Director of Law
